reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides speculative Dogecoin and broader crypto-market commentary using charts and personal price predictions. The community invitation and exchange referral are described as promotional components with disclosed affiliate commissions, trading risks, and no guarantee. Although it mentions a return figure, trade-copying invitation, and deposit-bonus claim, the available video evidence does not establish deception, victim loss, unfulfilled terms, or misconduct by the linked services.

citations.quote: in this video we're going to be talking about dogecoin why i bought dogecoin why i think it's going to go up
When Bitcoin is down 50%, that's essentially when you want to start buying.
i think dogecoin could go to a dollar this time
I personally have a million coins of Dogecoin.
make a million dollars from a hundred thousand dollar investment.

opening.argument: Judge the price claim together with the requested action. The speaker says Dogecoin could reach a dollar, describes what that would mean for his own investment, then invites viewers to join his community to copy his exact trades. That turns a forecast into a participation pitch: the audience is offered a way to follow the person presenting the large potential return. His warning that the outcome is not guaranteed qualifies the pitch, but does not separate the return from the invitation to act.

citations.quote: i think dogecoin could go to a dollar this time
make a million dollars from a hundred thousand dollar investment.
if you guys want to follow and copy my exact trades you're going to want to join my community today
dogecoin is not guaranteed to do anything

rebuttal.rebuttal: The charts and personal phrasing explain how the forecast is presented, but they do not answer what the forecast is used to sell. The speaker moves from his potential million-dollar outcome to asking viewers to copy his trades through his community. Nor does the absence of documented victim loss settle whether that solicitation should be treated as suspect; the concern is the promise-action relationship visible in the video.

citations.quote: make a million dollars from a hundred thousand dollar investment.
if you guys want to follow and copy my exact trades you're going to want to join my community today

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted forecast is conditional and explicitly personal, not a promised return for anyone who joins. The speaker expressly says Dogecoin is not guaranteed to do anything, and the description discloses trading risk and no guaranteed profits. An invitation to copy trades may be promotional, but these excerpts do not show deceptive terms or a guaranteed outcome.

opening.argument: Consider the signals in combination: viewers hear a $1,000 deposit-bonus claim tied to signing up through the speaker's link, are told they can use leverage, and are directed to a trading referral destination. The description separately acknowledges that some links earn commissions. The bonus makes the sign-up sound immediately rewarding, while leverage invites exposure to the very trading risks disclosed elsewhere. That combination warrants scrutiny as a reward-led solicitation, even without assuming the bonus is fictitious.

citations.quote: you guys can get a $1,000 deposit bonus if you sign up using my link below
It also has the cheapest fees and you can use leverage
Blofin: https://partner.blofin.com/d/MylesG
Some links are affiliate links (we may earn commissions).

rebuttal.rebuttal: Disclosing affiliate commissions does not remove the incentive behind the referral; it confirms that one may exist. The risk disclaimer also does not explain the conditions for receiving the advertised deposit bonus. The defense is right that the record does not prove an unfulfilled offer. But its account of the video as chiefly commentary underweights a specific bonus tied to signing up through the speaker's link.

citations.quote: Some links are affiliate links (we may earn commissions).
you guys can get a $1,000 deposit bonus if you sign up using my link below

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The bonus is described as a deposit bonus, not free cash for merely clicking a link, and the cited material does not establish that its terms are false or concealed. The description identifies affiliate links and warns that crypto trading can result in total loss. Leverage and a referral make this a consequential promotion, but they do not by themselves establish a scam.

opening.argument: The market discussion also serves a sales path. After arguing that crypto is near a bottom and that altcoins are about to rally, the speaker presents Dogecoin's possible rise to a dollar. He then tells viewers they can join his community to copy his trades; the description advertises VIP access with trade alerts and mentoring. The charts may be sincere analysis, but they give the trade-copying invitation its appeal. Assess the video as a pitch for participation built around anticipated token appreciation, not solely as detached market news.

i think dogecoin could go to a dollar this time
if you guys want to follow and copy my exact trades you're going to want to join my community today
Private Community - Trade Alerts - Mentoring - Training (Whop) Join VIP for full Access

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense cites the chart discussion and the speaker's personal predictions, but those do not make the subsequent invitation incidental. He explicitly links his trading history to an offer to copy his trades, while the description markets access to trade alerts. A disclaimer can qualify the forecast; it cannot erase the promotional role the forecast plays.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is present, but the speaker also spends substantial time explaining his market thesis, including what he sees as a Dogecoin chart breakout. He frames the dollar target as his belief and expressly denies any guarantee. The invitation to join a community does not show that its trade alerts are false, that viewers are promised appreciation, or that the linked service fails to deliver.
